unit.why: A short narrative: the narrator's father asks the Seer of Lublin to pray for a son, accepts the condition that he will not live long with him, and receives a yihud to draw down the narrator's soul.

stories.start_quote: עו״ש בכת״י כשהי׳ אבי הצדיק אצל
stories.end_quote: בעת היחוד להוריד נשמתי וכו׳ עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: The narrator's father begs the Seer of Lublin for a son; the Seer says that if he decrees it the son will be born but the father will not live long with him; the father accepts, and the Seer gives him an awesome yihud and holy names to concentrate on at union, in order to bring down the narrator's soul.

tags.why: The tale tells of the miraculous conception of the narrator, himself a tzaddik.

quotes: שיבקש רחמים עליו שיהי׳ לו בן זכר
tags.why: A son is granted through the tzaddik's intercession.

quotes: ומסר לו יחוד נורא ושמות קדושים
tags.why: The Seer transmits a kabbalistic yihud.
Holy names are used to draw down a soul.
Contemplative concentration with names during the act.
Mystical intentions are assigned to a ritual act.

quotes: ומסר לו יחוד נורא ושמות קדושים
tags.why: Mystical knowledge is used for a concrete result, a conception.

quotes: אבל לא תאריך ימים להיות עמו ביחד
tags.why: The Seer foretells the father's short life with his son; fulfilment is implied, not narrated.

quotes: שבהכרח אם אגזור שיהי׳ לך בן זכר יהי'
tags.why: The tzaddik's power to decree is asserted.

quotes: כשהי׳ אבי הצדיק אצל מורינו קדוש אלקי ישראל מלובלין
tags.why: The father is at the Seer's court with a request.
The narrator-tzaddik's father is the protagonist.

quotes: אצל מורינו קדוש אלקי ישראל מלובלין
tags.why: The father is a follower of the Seer.
The marital union is the occasion for the yihud.
The story is framed as quoted from a manuscript written by the narrator.

missing_concepts: drawing down a specific soul at conception
trade-off of the father's lifespan for a child
quotation from a manuscript (כתב יד) as the source
